tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H15): Library pipeline: custom dwconv+LN, cuBLASLt FP16 GEMMs with fused bias/residual, fp16 hidden, strided-batched NCHW output. Build a C++ solution (languages cuda_cpp + cublas; add -lcublasLt -lcublas to ld_flags; binding.cpp + kernel.cu layout; the cuBLASLt handle, matmul descriptors and the per-shape algorithm table are module-level caches keyed on (B,C,H,W) only, created on first call with cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic and never re-tuned). Launch sequence per call, identical for a given shape: K1 custom: depthwise 7x7 conv + bias + LayerNorm -> A1 fp16 [M][C] row-major (use zero-padded smem planes per warp for W<=14, register patches or TMA-free float4 rows otherwise; LN needs all C per token so tile tokens x all channels); extra blocks of K1 convert W1 -> fp16 [4C][C] and W2 -> fp16 [C][4C] with cvt.rn.f16x2 and compute b2' = b2 + W2*gb (GEMV). GEMM1: cublasLtMatmul fp16 x fp16, fp32 compute, BIAS epilogue (b1), output fp16 or fp32 [M][4C] (fp16 only if run_tests passes 16/16; report max err both ways). K2 custom: exact erf GELU (erff, not tanh), write h fp16 [M][4C], per-(image,k) sum of squares via warp reduce + atomics into a [B][4C] fp32 workspace zeroed by K1. K3 custom: s_b[k] = 1 + gw[k]*sqrt(gf2)/(mean_k sqrt(gf2) + eps) and apply it: when B*C*4C*2 bytes <= 16 MB write W2_b = W2*diag(s_b) fp16 per image, else scale h rows in place (half2). GEMM2: strided-batched cublasLtMatmul computing D_b^T [C][HW] = W2_b [C][4C] x h_b^T so D lands directly in NCHW, beta=1 with C operand = x_b (stride C*HW) and D = output_b, bias b2' per output channel (either in the epilogue or pre-added to the C operand by K1 writing output = x + b2' and using beta=1 with C == D). All workspaces from torch.empty in run(). Then measure, under harness timing on the rented B200: (1) per-launch times at 1,192,28,28; 2,768,7,7; 32,768,7,7; 32,128,64,64; 64,96,112,112; (2) for GEMM1/GEMM2 at every one of the 16 shapes, the top-3 heuristic algorithms, FP16 operands vs CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32 on the fp32 A1/W (no conversion kernel): pick the faster per shape into the table and record both; (3) the H16 probe: a kernel that writes then reads back a 20, 42 and 134 MB fp16 scratch after the harness's 2xL2 zero-fill, versus the same kernel with no scratch, to price the hidden round trip per size. run_tests on all 16 workloads x 10 rounds; report per-workload rented times, not band geomeans. Success: 16/16 pass; rented time <= 40 us on every S/M row (1,192 .. 2,768), <= 80 us at 8/16/32,768,7,7, <= 700 us at the largest; run_tests projected portal score >= 0.60; the per-launch breakdown and the H15/H16 numbers are recorded as findings. Refuted if: cuBLASLt GEMM1+GEMM2 together exceed 20 us at the S shapes for every heuristic algorithm (then the library floor caps the lineage near 0.6 and r2 replaces the GEMMs with custom tensor-core kernels), or the H16 probe shows the fp16 hidden round trip costs > 10 us at 8,320,32,32. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Experiment E2 (tests H12): Anchor with mma.sync FP16 GEMM cores, fp16 transposed weights and the measured phase-1 fixes; probes for the HMMA rate, the fixed floor, coop vs three launches and split-K. Step 0 (<= 10 min): microbench mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f32.f16.f16.f32 throughput on the rented B200: 148 CTAs x 4 and 8 warps, each warp running 8+ independent accumulator chains from registers, timed with clock64 and %globaltimer; report FLOP/clk/SM and PF/s at 1.5 GHz, and record it as a finding whatever the result (H12). Step 1, phase 1 of the anchor: switch transpose_mat to the measured warp-level transposes and emit fp16 W1t [C][4C] and W2t [4C][C] (cvt.rn); for W <= 14 use the zero-padded smem-plane dwconv (measured 35.5 us at 32,768,7,7); keep xn fp32 K-major [C][Mp] and the LN partial sums. Step 2, GEMM phases: keep the CTA tiles (128x128, 128x96, 64x64, 32x32), 8 warps, BK=32 and the register double-buffering, but store A as fp16 [k][m] (affine applied per element in fp32 before cvt.rn.f16x2, as now) and B from the fp16 Wt into padded smem, load fragments with ldmatrix (.trans where the layout needs it) and accumulate with mma.sync m16n8k16 in fp32; keep the exact-erf GELU epilogue, write the hidden as fp16 [4C][Mp] (halves P2 store and P3 load traffic; it is the GEMM2 operand rounding already simulated), keep per-image sumsq atomics, split-K and the x+b2 output init. Keep registers <= 128 so 2 CTAs/SM stay resident. Step 3 probes under harness timing, 3 interleaved repeats each: (a) the fixed floor F: this kernel with all three phases stubbed to a trivial write (grid syncs intact) at 1,192,28,28 and 2,768,7,7; (b) H4: the same phase code as one cooperative launch vs three plain launches at 1,192,28,28, 2,768,7,7 and 64,96,112,112, recording regs per phase kernel; (c) H5: split3 forced to 1 vs auto at 2,768,7,7, 8,768,7,7 and 1,192,28,28; (d) a per-phase breakdown at 1,192,28,28 and 1,160,449,7. run_tests on all 16 workloads x 10 rounds; report per-workload rented times. Success: 16/16 pass; rented <= 45 us on every S row, <= 60 us at 2,768,7,7, <= 150 us at 32,768,7,7, <= 2500 us at the largest; projected portal score >= 0.55; F, the HMMA rate, the coop-vs-3-launch and split-K numbers recorded as findings. Refuted if: mma.sync FP16 throughput < 0.15 PF/s at 1.5 GHz with the GEMM phases still > 100 us at 32,768,7,7 (then B moves to a tcgen05 engine in r2), or the stubbed-phase floor F > 15 us (then one cooperative launch with grid syncs cannot reach S ~0.85 and B's thesis changes to counters/dataflow). Experiment E3 (tests H13): Cluster-per-image kernel for the 7x7 and 14x14 rows (hidden slices in smem, DSMEM reductions, no grid barrier), with cluster-occupancy, DSMEM and TFLOAT32-rounding probes; other shapes dispatched to the anchor path. Step 0 probes (<= 20 min, record each as a finding): (a) cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters for cluster sizes 8 and 16 (cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed) with 200 KB dynamic smem and 256 threads per CTA: how many clusters run concurrently and the launch-to-first-instruction latency under harness timing; (b) DSMEM microbench in clocks: 16 CTAs all-gather a 75 KB fp16 tile (each writes its 1/16 into every CTA via st.shared::cluster) and reduce-scatter 16 x [768 x 49] fp32 partials (each CTA reads 15 slices via ld.shared::cluster); (c) H14: TMA-load fp32 values with chosen low mantissa bits through a TFLOAT32 tensor map and check bit-exactly whether the result is round-to-nearest or truncation. If (a) gives fewer than 6 concurrent 16-CTA clusters, use 8-CTA clusters (two clusters per image pair is not allowed; use 8 slices of 4C/8). Step 1 kernel, for 2/8/16/32,768,7,7 and 8/16,384,14,14 (dispatch every other shape to the anchor's cooperative kernel copied from the r0 baseline): one cluster per image (two 7x7 images per cluster when B >= 8), CTA j owns C/G channels for the dwconv (zero-padded smem planes) and hidden slice j of 4C/G. LN: per-token partial sums exchanged through DSMEM (one cluster barrier), each CTA normalises its channels and writes the fp16 a tile [tokens][C] into every CTA's smem via st.shared::cluster (second barrier). GEMM1 swap-AB: A = W1 slice [4C/G x C] (fp32 from global/L2 converted to fp16 in smem, or TF32 if (c) confirms rounding), B = a^T, N = tokens; use whichever engine you can get correct in the session (mma.sync FP16 is acceptable; tcgen05 is not required for the thesis). GELU (exact erf) in registers; gf_k = sqrt(sum over tokens of h^2) is thread-local per hidden channel; one DSMEM reduce of the per-CTA partial sums of gf gives mean_k gf (third barrier); s_k = 1 + gw_k*gf_k/(mean+eps), h' = s_k*h + gb_k in registers, written fp16 to the CTA's own smem. GEMM2 partial: W2[:, slice] [C x 4C/G] x h'^T -> [C x tokens] fp32; reduce across the cluster by DSMEM reduce-scatter (CTA j finalises output channels j*C/G .. (j+1)*C/G: + b2 + x, store NCHW with lanes along hw). Weights: each CTA reads only its two slices (1.2 MB at C=768) and ideally once per cluster via TMA multicast or plain L2 reads; measure which. Time each phase in clocks for one cluster at 32,768,7,7 and compare with the 12 us kill criterion from the probe. run_tests on all 16 workloads x 10 rounds; report per-workload rented times. Success: 16/16 pass; rented <= 30 us at 2,768,7,7 and 8,768,7,7, <= 45 us at 16,768,7,7 and 32,768,7,7, <= 40 us at 8/16,384,14,14 (anchor: 124-1217 us); projected portal score >= 0.50 with the other 10 rows still on the anchor path; probe numbers (concurrent clusters, DSMEM gather/reduce clocks, TFLOAT32 rounding) recorded. Refuted if: fewer than 4 concurrent 8-CTA clusters, or weight-slice ingest plus one GEMM1 per CTA > 12 us at 32,768,7,7 under harness timing, or DSMEM all-gather of the 75 KB a tile > 3 us; any of these means the cluster path cannot beat ~30 us per row and the lineage is retired after incubation with the probe numbers as its conclusions.
